input.command: make build && make unit && make component 2>&1 | tail -150

answer:
**Not all checks pass.** One unit test fails, on both target frameworks. I changed no files.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `make build` | Passed. It printed only NU1902 warnings about `Scriban.Signed` 7.2.0. |
| `make unit` | **Failed**: 1 failed and 271 passed out of 272, on both net10.0 and net9.0. |
| `make component` | Skipped by the `&&` chain. I ran it on its own and 20 of 20 passed on net10.0. |

**Failing test:** `ConfIT.UnitTest.Util.DeltaFormatterTests.Format_FieldInActualNotInExpected_ShowsAbsentSentinel` (`test/ConfIT.UnitTest/Util/DeltaFormatterTests.cs:53`). It fails the same way on net10.0 and net9.0, so there is one cause.

The test expects the output to contain the sentinel `<absent>`, but the formatter now prints `<not present>`. The assertion message was:

```
Expected result "...Response body mismatch:
debug
  expected: <not present>
  actual:   "trace"" to contain "<absent>".
```

This looks like the test and `DeltaFormatter` disagree about the sentinel text. I haven't checked which one is out of date.

The `make component` run is a separate run, and I didn't check which framework it targeted. The output shows it built and ran only net10.0, even though the project targets net9.0 as well.
